newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fresh riot breaks out in Indonesia's Pekalongan.
newsitem.headline: Fresh riot breaks out in Indonesia's Pekalongan.

text.p: A motor cycle dealership was looted and one person stabbed in fresh disturbances on Sunday near Pekalongan town in Indonesia's populous Central Java province, police and residents said.

Second Sergaent Sukarti from Buaran just outside Pekalongan, 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta, said police were investigating the early morning incident, which appeared to be linked to rioting there two weeks ago.
"It's true we had a riot. It was probably connected with the events last week," he told Reuters by telephone from Buaran, adding that so far there had been no arrests.
The situation had returned to normal by daybreak, he said.

Sukarti said it appeared the distrubance started after a youth who is a supporter of the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP) was stabbed by an unknown assailant. It was not clear when the assault took place, he said.

An agitated crowd gathered on Saturday night after prayers. Early on Sunday they broke into a motorcycle dealership owned by an ethnic Chinese and took seven motor bikes onto the street and burnt them, he added. One resident said eight bikes were burnt.
Residents said the 300-400 rioters also felled trees and power poles, blocking a number of roads, and emptied rubbish bins onto the roads.

They said the crowd was angry over news that a popular local religious leader had been summonsed by police in the provincial capital Semarang to investigate allegations that he masterminded the recent rioting.
The Kompas daily on Sunday quoted Central Java police as saying they had summoned the religious leader on Saturday because they had proof, including recordings of his speeches.

The official Antara news agency quoted Religious Affairs Minister Tarmizi Taher on Sunday as saying there was evidence the Pekalongan rioting was triggered by a religious leader who lacked a "broad national insight." He did not elaborate.
Last week, 30 people were detained from three days to three months for their involvement in the March 26 riot when a number of shops and properties of local ethnic Chinese were vandalised.

Residents said that riot started when PPP flags were removed by supporters of the ruling Golkar party before a popular singer, who used to campaign for PPP but is now a Golkar candidate, and an Islamic preacher were due to visit the area.
